title: Group Membership area: restricted groups with members and memberof directions

provenance.note: Shape derived from Microsoft security-template documentation for restricted groups. SID-star syntax follows the certified Privilege Rights precedent in the WP-3 tranche (principals as *S-1-5-...), which is native-observed; the __Members/__Memberof key suffixes are spec-informed until captured.

anchors.note: Certified WP-3 tranche evidence; natively proves the *SID principal syntax this area shares with Privilege Rights.

operator_meaning: Administrators (S-1-5-32-544) has exactly Backup Operators (S-1-5-32-551) and Local System (S-1-5-18) as members
Backup Operators is a member of Administrators

derivations: The restricted-group key is the group SID in star form with a __Members or __Memberof suffix; the value is a comma-separated star-SID list. The star-SID syntax itself is native-observed via the certified Privilege Rights tranche.
__Members and __Memberof are independent directions with different semantics (replace membership vs. add this group to another); a typed Studio model must keep them distinct.
Well-known SID strings are used so the template is lab-portable without a migration table; a domain-principal variant is a follow-up scenario once this one passes.

open_questions: Does secedit /export return group SIDs, group names, or a mixture, and does the answer differ for well-known versus domain SIDs?
Is an empty __Members value the documented way to strip all members, and does /export render it as an empty assignment?
Does /validate reject a __Memberof cycle (A memberof B, B memberof A) or is the cycle only an endpoint-processing concern?
